::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Indefinite Integral: $\int sec^{n}x dx$](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2553240/indefinite-integral-int-secnx-dx), asked by [sergio.azevedo](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/474746/sergio-azevedo) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2017-12-06; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> How do I show that
>
> $$\int \sec^{n}(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \frac{1}{n-1}\sec^{n-2}(x)\tan(x) + \frac{n-2}{n-1}\int \sec^{n-2}(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$$
:::

Peel off two factors of secant:
$$\sec^n x = \sec^{n-2} x \cdot\sec^2 x$$
Now integrate by parts with $u=\sec^{n-2} x$ and $dv = \sec^2 x\,dx$.  Rearrange making use of the formula
$$\tan^2 x = \sec^2 x - 1$$
